title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1RC0RA_1LD1LA_1RE1LD_---1RF_0RD1RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1RC0RA_1LD1LA_1RE1LD_---1RF_0RD1RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

Seen at the moments the head, in state B, reaches a new cell on the right, the tape is mostly a row of digits: blocks 1^(4m+1) 0, one more than a multiple of four ones each followed by a single 0, read as the numbers m. In the run of 2·1010 steps 74 of the 103 such moments have exactly this form (the others hold a block of 4m+2 ones, which appears at the visits to the left end and lingers). Most digits are 0. Near the right end a big block grows by four ones at every second new right cell, and the time between new right cells doubles; meanwhile a digit 1 walks left through the 0s, one place per record. It is the same kind of machine as 1RB---_1RC1RF_1LD1RE_1LB1LD_0RB0RC_1RA0LF.

At each new cell on the right in state B the tape is mostly a list of digits 1^(4m+1) 0, most of them 0, then a big block of ones, then 0 1 0 1 B>0. The new cells come in pairs a few steps apart and then a long pause, during which the head runs to the left end, rewrites the list (in the middle of a period the digits look scrambled and the big block is cut into pieces) and comes back with the list restored and the big block four 1s longer. The pause doubles from one period to the next.
verdict: The question is open. The machine halts exactly from F> 0 0 0 (both directions in Lean). The run is a sequence of periods: in each the head goes to the left end and back, and at the right end the big block grows by four 1s (a 21-step rule proved in Lean). The periods double: 459,930, 919,858, ..., 58,870,786 steps, each exactly twice the previous minus 2, and later 3,759,931,386 and 7,519,862,778 steps, with occasional larger corrections when the digits near the left end change. F has met 0 0 1 only at steps 257, 11,457, 16,839,809 and 2,371,684,619, the only times up to that step (5 times in 1010 steps by the ctxcount census), each time just after a long block was written at the very left end of the tape; the halt needs a 0 where those near misses had the 1.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 241 cells have been visited and 183 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/exp
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.051). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.105).

claims.title: The halting context
claims.text: From F> 0 0 0 the machine reaches its halting transition (proved step by step, then step_none_iff). The halting transition is E reading a 0. E is entered only from D reading a 0 (D writes 1 and moves right), and D is entered from C or D moving left (so the cell D's 1 would hand to E is the 1 they just wrote) or from F reading a 0 and moving right. So the only way to halt is F> 0 0 0, and F itself comes only from E reading a 1. The converse is proved: a configuration halts two steps later if and only if it is F> 0 0 0 (halt_iff_2), so a halting run from blank passes through it (halts_blank_pred_2).

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: 8 shift rules over the words of the tape (for example (1)^n D> 1 becomes D> 1 (1)^n in n steps, 0 D> (10)^n becomes (11)^n 0 D> in 2n steps), proved for every n.

claims.title: No halt in the first 20,000,000,000 steps
claims.text: tools/c/tmrun.c runs 20,000,000,000 steps without a halt; the visited tape is 265 cells wide and holds 208 ones.

claims.title: Near misses
claims.text: F had 0 0 1 ahead of it only 5 times in the first 1010 steps (the last at step 2,372,144,797, at a visit to the left end) and never 0 0 0.

claims.title: The macro configuration
claims.text: At 74 of the 103 new right cells reached in state B in 2·1010 steps every inner block of the tape is 1^(4m+1) 0.

claims.title: Binary clock
claims.text: Between consecutive new right cells the time doubles (for example 58,870,786, 117,741,564, 235,483,274, 470,953,978, 941,907,956 steps between steps 1.3·10<sup>8</sup> and 1.9·10<sup>9</sup>).

claims.title: The step at the right end
claims.text: L 1 0 1 0 1 0 1 1 C> 0^inf reaches L 1 1 1 1 1 0 1 0 1 B> 0^inf in 21 steps: the big block absorbs 0 1 0 and the tail moves two cells right (the pair of records at the end of each period).

claims.title: Where the near misses are
claims.text: F reads 0 with 0 1 after it at steps 257, 11,457, 16,839,809 and 2,371,684,619 and at no other step up to 2,371,684,619; each time the tape begins with a block 1^6, 1^26, 1^38, 1^54 just written at its left end, then F>0 0 1 0 1 0 1 .... The halt is the same picture with 0 0 0.

claims.title: No halt in the first 30,000,000,000 steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/tmrun.c runs 3·1010 steps without a halt; 264 cells visited (last new cell).

claims.title: No small finite-automata certificate
claims.text: A finite-automata-reduction search (a DFA of n states on one side of the head, the least co-closed NFA on (state × DFA state) + bottom for the other) finds no certificate with n ≤ 6, with the DFA on the left or on the right.

claims.title: The clock test
claims.text: At the visits of the right end in state C on a 0 the tape is W 14n+1 0 1 0 1 1 C>0. From the visit at step 16,962,494 (n = 8), the word W at each later visit of the phase is the word at the visit before after 2k applications of one base map, up to 214 applications (the visit at step 252,438,652). This is the clock of the machines of holdouts/1RB0RA_0LC0RE_1LE1LD_0LE---_1LF0LC_1RA1LE, found by running the machine; its tick is not proved (the head works through the block like a counter, which is not the sweep–trip–merge template of gen_clock.py).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: What exactly does one period do to the list (the doubling says it runs through all the values of a counter of growing length), and can the left end ever give F three 0s? The near misses become rarer (steps 257, 11,457, 16,839,809, 2,371,684,619).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine has run 20,000,000,000 steps without stopping. Its tape is a row of digits, each a block of ones one more than a multiple of four; a carry walks along the row while the time to the next new cell doubles. It can stop only from one local pattern, F> 0 0 0, which it has never produced.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 265 cells visited.
Every halt passes through it, and it always halts (Lean: halt_ctx, halt_iff_2).
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: The one way to stop
html: The halting transition is E reading a 0. E is entered only from D reading a 0 (D writes 1 and moves right), and D is entered from C or D moving left (so the cell D's 1 would hand to E is the 1 they just wrote) or from F reading a 0 and moving right. So the only way to halt is F> 0 0 0, and F itself comes only from E reading a 1. So the machine halts exactly when it produces F> 0 0 0; Lean proves both directions (halt_ctx: the steps from there to the halt; halt_iff_2: nothing else halts two steps later).

sections.heading: What a proof would need
html: Not known. As long as the tape keeps the form of a digit row, F never finds three 0s in a row at the places it is entered; what is missing is the rule of the row (the walk of the carry, what the visits to the left end do), from which one could prove the form is kept.

The basic moves are proved in Lean for every length (lean/Rules.lean: crossing a run of one word in a fixed number of steps per copy), so a proof would need only the rule of the counter on top of them.

sections.heading: Periods that double
html: At the right end of the tape the machine writes in short bursts: two new cells, 21 steps (a rule proved in Lean), two more, and then a long pause. During the pause the head travels to the left end and back and rewrites everything in between; when it returns, the list of digits is usually as before and the big block at the right end has four more 1s. The pauses, from the run (steps):

From 459,930 to 58,870,786 each pause is exactly twice the previous one minus 2. Doubling pauses are the signature of a binary counter: each period the head counts through all values of a counter that has one more digit than in the previous period.

sections.heading: Near misses at the left end
html: The halt needs F, moving right, to read three 0s in a row: then D gets a 0, writes a 1 and hands E a 0, the missing transition. The first four times F read 0 0 1 (up to step 2,371,684,619) were all at the very left end of the tape, just after the head wrote a long block there:
One more 0 at the start of the list would be a halt. The near misses come at steps 257, 11,457, 16,839,809 and 2,371,684,619, ever more rarely.

sections.heading: 2<sup>k</sup> applications of one map
html: At the visits of the right end in state C the tape is W 14n+1 0 1 0 1 1 C>0, n growing by one per visit. From the visit at step 16,962,494 (n = 8), the word W at each later visit of the phase is the word at the visit before after 2k applications of one base map, up to 214 applications (the visit at step 252,438,652). That is the clock of five other holdouts, where it is proved in Lean; here only the test by running the machine is done.

summary: A list of digits 1^(4m+1) 0 with a big block at the right end that gains four 1s per period while the period doubles; the only near misses of the halt (F> 0 0 1) come right after visits to the left end.
